phone.description: a phone number, as a component of what it reaches — on a person, their mobile, beside the `email{address}` they wear

sms_consent.description: a person agreed to be texted at their `phone{number}`, in these words; removed when they stop texts

person.description: who agreed; the eid is derived from it, so a person has one consent

consent.description: the words they agreed to, exactly as they were shown

space.description: the space whose Operator texts them: the one they agreed on, and where a text from them goes

text.description: one text message, sent or received; its words are `doc{body}`. One with @yaks/mail's `deliver{to}` asks to be sent to the `phone{number}` of `deliver.to`, and its outcome is `delivered` or `bounced`

from.description: the number it came from, in E.164 form; absent on one to send, which goes from the sender's own

to.description: the number it went to, or the RCS agent's id for an RCS text that arrived; written on one sent once it leaves

message_id.description: the provider's id for it: read from one that arrived, or returned by the sender for one that left

rcs.description: whether it came, or goes, as RCS rather than SMS

text_post.description: Hand an outbound text to the sender and record its outcome. A send the sender knows never left is tried again.
